title: Curvefield — Elliptic-Curve Cryptography Lab
description: An interactive ECC lab: the geometric group law, finite-field curves, a from-scratch secp256k1 cryptosystem (ECDSA + BIP-340 Schnorr + MuSig2), Curve25519, and a hand-written BLS12-381 pairing — now standards-grade and the substrate for a from-scratch Groth16 zk-SNARK. RFC 9380 hash-to-curve (expand_message_xmd, Simplified SWU with the 11-/3-isogenies, cofactor clearing) reproduces the RFC's own G1/G2 test vectors; ZCash/Ethereum point serialization, IRTF BLS signatures with HKDF KeyGen (matching the EIP-2333 vector) and proof-of-possession, and an optimized Hayashida–Aranha final exponentiation round out a production-shaped pairing stack. The Groth16 lab proves knowledge of a secret (x³+x+5=out) in three group elements, verified by one pairing equation, and a from-scratch PLONK lab proves the *same* statement with a universal setup — selector-gate arithmetization, a copy-constraint permutation argument, a grand-product polynomial, and a transparent KZG-batched verifier — so the two SNARKs sit side by side. From-scratch BULLETPROOFS add a Fiat–Shamir inner-product argument that folds the witness in half each round, giving aggregated logarithmic range proofs (a 64-bit amount in ~16 group elements, ~20× smaller than the linear form) checked by both a transparent and an optimized single-multiexp verifier, plus a full confidential transaction — homomorphic kernel-excess balance over an aggregated range proof, the Monero/Mimblewimble structure, with an inflation attack shown to break it. Plus Schnorr adaptor signatures and atomic swaps, BIP-32 HD wallets, Shamir/Feldman secret sharing, FROST threshold signatures, zero-knowledge Σ-protocols (Pedersen, Chaum–Pedersen, range proofs), KZG polynomial commitments, and discrete-log + invalid-curve attacks. A from-scratch STARK rounds out the proof-system shelf: the one system here that needs no elliptic curve and no trusted setup — transparent and plausibly post-quantum, resting on a hash alone. It proves an actual execution (a Fibonacci-square recurrence) over the Goldilocks field p = 2⁶⁴ − 2³² + 1 with a hand-written NTT, Merkle commitments, a Fiat–Shamir transcript, DEEP out-of-domain sampling, and a full FRI low-degree test — and demonstrates soundness live by rejecting a forged intermediate step. A VERIFIABLE RANDOM FUNCTION lab implements ECVRF (RFC 9381) on Edwards25519 in both ciphersuites — try-and-increment and the constant-time Elligator2 map — reproducing the RFC's own proof (π) test vectors byte-for-byte and driving a verifiable leader-election lottery. A LINKABLE RING SIGNATURE lab builds Monero's anonymity core from scratch — SAG, bLSAG, and the concise CLSAG with key images I = x·Hₚ(P), plus CryptoNote stealth one-time addresses — assembled into a complete private payment that hides the sender yet still catches a double-spend. A SEALED secure-channel lab closes the one missing dimension — confidentiality — by assembling the whole engine into the SIGNAL PROTOCOL, the end-to-end encryption behind WhatsApp and Signal: a from-scratch ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 8439, pinned byte-for-byte), HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869), XEdDSA prekey signatures, X3DH key agreement with an offline recipient, and the Double Ratchet that gives every message forward secrecy and heals the session one round trip after a full key compromise — driven by a live Alice⇄Bob chat you can tamper with, reorder, and compromise. A POST-QUANTUM lattice lab adds ML-KEM (FIPS 203, the standardised CRYSTALS-Kyber) built entirely from scratch — a hand-written Keccak/SHA-3 + SHAKE sponge (pinned to the FIPS 202 digests), the negacyclic number-theoretic transform over Z₃₃₂₉[X]/(X²⁵⁶+1) with a base multiply pinned to a schoolbook convolution, centered-binomial noise, Compress/Decompress ciphertext coding, and the Fujisaki–Okamoto transform with implicit rejection — for all three parameter sets (ML-KEM-512/768/1024), matching the standard's key and ciphertext byte-sizes exactly and demonstrating IND-CCA2 by catching a mauled ciphertext; wired into the real TLS 1.3 X25519MLKEM768 hybrid handshake so a classical curve and a lattice KEM secure one session together. Its companion, ML-DSA (FIPS 204, the standardised CRYSTALS-Dilithium), completes the post-quantum story with the mainstream lattice SIGNATURE that retires ECDSA/Ed25519/BLS — a from-scratch Fiat–Shamir-with-aborts scheme over Z₈₃₈₀₄₁₇[X]/(X²⁵⁶+1): a full 256-point NTT (the ring splits completely), Power2Round/Decompose and the MakeHint/UseHint carry-recovery mechanism (each pinned by its round-trip identity), the ExpandA/ExpandS/ExpandMask samplers and the τ-sparse SampleInBall challenge, byte-exact packing with a validating hint decoder, and the rejection-sampling signing loop that keeps the response independent of the secret — for all three parameter sets (ML-DSA-44/65/87), matching the standard's exact key and signature byte-sizes and rejecting any tampered message, mauled signature, or wrong key, with a lab that lays the abort loop bare (live iteration count, per-attempt rejection reasons, the sparse ±1 challenge, and the response histogram) — plus HashML-DSA (the FIPS 204 §5.4 pre-hash mode over SHA-512 or SHAKE-256, cryptographically bound to its hash's DER OID), deterministic-vs-hedged signing, and a rejection-loop iteration histogram. A SECURE-COMPUTATION lab opens a whole new pillar — computing on inputs two parties never share — with Yao's two-party protocol built from scratch: a Chou–Orlandi oblivious transfer on this lab's Ed25519 group (the sender never learns the receiver's choice; the receiver opens only one message), then garbled circuits with the free-XOR and half-gate optimizations (XOR and NOT are free; an AND costs the proven-minimal two ciphertexts) over 128-bit labels from the lab's own SHA-256. It runs Yao's original Millionaires' Problem — who is richer, revealing nothing else — plus private equality, sum, product, and a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction — learn the winner and the price, never the bids — each with an auditable transcript and a live single-byte-tamper integrity demo, verified exhaustively against a plaintext oracle over every 4-bit input pair; and, as a second paradigm on the same circuits, the GMW protocol (secret sharing instead of garbling — wires kept XOR-shared, each AND gate resolved by a 1-of-4 oblivious transfer), cross-checked to reconstruct the identical result. A VERIFIABLE DELAY FUNCTION lab adds the time analogue of the VRF — proof of *sequential* work: y = x^(2^T) mod N over a 512-bit Blum RSA group takes T squarings that no parallelism can shorten, yet verifies in one shot via BOTH the succinct Wesolowski proof (a single group element and a Fiat–Shamir hash-to-prime ℓ, checked by π^ℓ·x^r = y) and the log-size Pietrzak halving proof (a recursive fold down to y = x², log₂T midpoints), each pinned against the trapdoor evaluation (e = 2^T mod φ(N), the shortcut that is exactly why a real modulus must be one nobody has factored — an RSA challenge number or a class group) and against forged proofs, mauled outputs, and the wrong delay — plus a Rivest–Shamir–Wagner time-lock puzzle that encrypts a message to the future (locked instantly with the trapdoor, opened only by grinding the full squaring chain live) and an unbiasable delay-based randomness beacon that chains VDF outputs each carrying a verifiable proof-of-time (the RANDAO+VDF / Chia proof-of-time shape). A companion CLASS-GROUP VDF closes the RSA construction's one gap — its trapdoor — by moving the whole Wesolowski machine into the CLASS GROUP OF AN IMAGINARY QUADRATIC ORDER Cl(Δ), a group of genuinely UNKNOWN ORDER WITH NO TRUSTED SETUP (the class number h(Δ) ≈ √|Δ| is believed as hard as factoring to compute, and Δ is just a public prime discriminant hashed from a seed, so unlike an RSA modulus nobody — not even its creator — holds a φ to shortcut the delay): binary quadratic forms (a,b,c) built from scratch on BigInt with Gauss reduction (the ρ operator, coordinates bounded by √(|Δ|/3) forever) and Gauss composition (Cohen Alg. 5.4.7), a canonical prime-form generator, y = g^(2^T) by T sequential class-group squarings, the one-form succinct proof π = g^⌊2^T/ℓ⌋ verified by π^ℓ ∘ g^r = y, an O(1)-memory streaming prover, and a no-trusted-setup delay beacon — the engine under Chia's consensus, validated against the group axioms on the FULL CAYLEY TABLE of small discriminants and the known class numbers h(−23)=3, h(−47)=5, h(−71)=7, h(−3299)=27. A DOUBLY-EFFICIENT INTERACTIVE-PROOF lab implements the SUM-CHECK PROTOCOL and GKR from scratch over the Goldilocks field — multilinear extensions and the ẽq Lagrange basis, the round-by-round univariate messages a verifier collapses with a single oracle evaluation instead of an exponential sum, and a Fiat–Shamir transcript — then layers it into the Goldwasser–Kalai–Rothblum protocol that certifies a whole layered arithmetic circuit's output while the verifier re-executes ZERO gates, reducing each layer to the next by one sum-check fused with the two-claim line-restriction trick and bottoming out at the public input's MLE; alongside the two canonical applications — verified n×n MATRIX MULTIPLICATION (check C = A·B from O(log n) interaction, never redoing the O(n³) product; Thaler §4.4) and TRIANGLE COUNTING (proving Σ Ã(x,y)Ã(y,z)Ã(z,x) = 6·#triangles with the adjacency MLE evaluated at just three points) — the interactive-proof machinery under Spartan, HyperPlonk and Jolt, with live soundness demos that catch a forged claimed sum, a forged product entry, an inflated triangle count, or a single tampered output wire. A capstone BALLOT lab finally wires the threshold and zero-knowledge shelves into the protocol they were invented for — HELIOS/BELENIOS end-to-end-VERIFIABLE VOTING, built entirely from the lab's own parts: EXPONENTIAL ELGAMAL on secp256k1 whose ciphertexts are ADDITIVELY HOMOMORPHIC (votes encoded in the exponent so a bulletin board tallies encrypted ballots and decrypts only the total, recovered by a bounded baby-step giant-step discrete log), a PEDERSEN (joint-Feldman) DISTRIBUTED KEY GENERATION that splits the decryption key t-of-n so no authority can decrypt, 1-of-k ballots each carrying a DISJUNCTIVE CHAUM–PEDERSEN proof that every slot encrypts a bit plus a DLEQ that the slots sum to exactly one vote (cast-as-intended, no ballot-stuffing), a homomorphic tally, THRESHOLD DECRYPTION where each trustee publishes a partial decryption with a DLEQ proof and any t combine by Lagrange in the exponent, and — the property real elections are graded on — a UNIVERSAL VERIFIER that re-derives the trustee keys from the public commitments and re-checks every ballot and decryption proof trusting no one and touching no secret, with live tamper toggles (ballot-stuffing, a dishonest trustee) it catches by name. A BBS ANONYMOUS-CREDENTIALS lab adds the multi-message signature the digital-identity world is standardising on (draft-irtf-cfrg-bbs-signatures — the crypto under W3C Verifiable Credentials, the ISO mobile driver's licence, and the EU Digital Identity Wallet), built from scratch on the lab's own BLS12-381 pairing: an issuer signs a VECTOR of attributes once (A = (P1 + domain·Q₁ + Σ mᵢ·Hᵢ)/(sk+e), verified by one pairing e(A, PK+e·P₂) = e(B, P₂)), and the holder later proves possession of that signature in ZERO KNOWLEDGE while DISCLOSING ONLY A CHOSEN SUBSET of attributes — a Fiat–Shamir Σ-proof over a randomized signature (Ā = r·A, D̂ = r·B − e·Ā, with the pairing e(Ā, PK) = e(D̂, P₂) surviving the randomization) that hides every undisclosed message and makes every presentation UNLINKABLE to every other, so a mobile driver's licence can prove OVER-21 to a bar without revealing name, date of birth, or the licence number that would let two bars recognise you, all with the issuer offline — with a live lab (disclose/hide toggles, an editable verifier session that catches replay, and a soundness panel that rejects a lied-about value, a tampered Ā, and a mauled response) and a soundness argument that extracts a genuine signature from any accepting proof — plus BLIND ISSUANCE, where the holder commits to hidden attributes (a device LINK SECRET the issuer must never learn) and proves the opening in zero knowledge, and the issuer completes the signature from the commitment, so the credential is bound to a secret only the holder's device knows yet the issuer, who signed it, still cannot impersonate or recognise the holder (the AnonCreds / mDL holder-binding story). A NOVA FOLDING-SCHEME lab adds the modern engine of INCREMENTALLY VERIFIABLE COMPUTATION (Kothapalli–Setty–Tzialla, 2022): to prove a step function F was applied N times — a hash chain, a VM loop, a rollup's blocks — Nova never proves each step, it FOLDS each into a running accumulator with one random linear combination. The trick is RELAXED R1CS, (A·Z)∘(B·Z) = u·(C·Z) + E, a shape closed under a random fold Z = Z₁ + r·Z₂ so the quadratic's cross terms land exactly in a computable T and are absorbed by u and E; because the from-scratch non-hiding PEDERSEN COMMITMENT on this lab's BLS12-381 𝔾₁ is additively homomorphic, the verifier folds the committed instances with a couple of curve additions and a scalar mul per commitment while never seeing a witness, and a Fiat–Shamir transcript picks the challenge so no commitment can be chosen after r. It builds the canonical Nova step z ↦ z³ + z + 5 as an R1CS, folds an N-step chain into ONE relaxed instance, and shows that a SINGLE relaxed-R1CS satisfaction check — instead of N ordinary ones — certifies the whole computation, with live soundness demos that reject a corrupted final witness, a forged cross-term commitment, and broken step-to-step chaining (no trusted setup, no pairings, no FFTs) — and, on the very same generic folding core, a second application that folds a MiMC-style arithmetic permutation (rounds of x ↦ (x+c)³) into a SEQUENTIAL HASH CHAIN, the MinRoot-VDF skeleton, proving a whole chain ran with one final check. A SLH-DSA lab completes the post-quantum signature story with the *conservative* alternative to ML-DSA — the standardised stateless HASH-BASED signature (FIPS 205, the SPHINCS⁺ NIST chose), built entirely on the lab's own from-scratch SHA-256 and resting on nothing but that hash's collision/pre-image resistance (the same and only assumption the STARK already makes — no lattice): the FIPS-205 address with its 22-byte ADRSc compression, the SHA-2 tweakable-hash family (PK.seed block-padded, an MGF1-SHA-256 message digest), WOTS⁺ one-time chains, an XMSS Merkle key, the d-layer hypertree, and a stateless FORS few-time signature whose leaf is chosen pseudo-randomly from the per-message randomiser — for the SHA-2 category-1 sets (SLH-DSA-SHA2-128f and -128s), matching the standard's exact 32-byte public key and 17088-/7856-byte signature sizes and reproducing NIST's own ACVP keyGen roots and sigGen signature digests byte-for-byte, with a live lab that lays the hypertree and FORS leaf-selection bare, counts every hash the signature costs, and catches a mauled byte, a wrong context, and a forged root. An AES & AUTHENTICATED-MODES lab finally adds the SYMMETRIC standard the internet actually runs on — the one primitive a curve-heavy lab was missing — built from the GF(2⁸) field up: AES-128/192/256 (FIPS-197) with an S-box COMPUTED as the multiplicative inverse composed with the affine map (log/exp tables over the generator 0x03, nothing tabled), the full key schedule and round transformations with a scrubbable round-by-round 4×4 state-matrix visualiser pinned to the FIPS-197 Appendix B trace and the Appendix C ciphertexts for all three key sizes; then the authenticated modes riding on it — AES-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D) with the GF(2¹²⁸) GHASH multiply built from the bit up and a live block-by-block accumulator, pinned to the McGrew–Viega test cases; AES-GCM-SIV (RFC 8452), the nonce-misuse-resistant AEAD whose POLYVAL is a direct Montgomery multiply (dot(a,b)=a·b·x⁻¹²⁸), shown side by side with GCM on the same core so the NONCE-REUSE CLIFF is visible (reuse a nonce and GCM's C₁⊕C₂ leaks P₁⊕P₂ outright while GCM-SIV survives); AES-SIV (RFC 5297), the CMAC-based deterministic AEAD beside GCM-SIV; AES-CCM (RFC 3610), Counter-with-CBC-MAC — the mandatory cipher of Wi-Fi WPA2, Bluetooth LE and Zigbee/Thread — so the shelf covers both mainstream AES AEADs and both misuse-resistant ones; and AES-CMAC (RFC 4493), the block-cipher MAC — every one matched byte-for-byte to its FIPS/NIST/RFC vectors, and AES-256-GCM wired into the Sealed channel as an interchangeable cipher suite so the whole X3DH + Double Ratchet runs over it, proving the record layer is cipher-agnostic. A LOOKUP-ARGUMENTS lab adds the third pillar of every modern PLONKish/zkVM system, next to PLONK's gates and permutation argument: proving a witness value lies in a fixed table in ONE constraint instead of re-deriving the operation with dozens of gates — the reason Halo2, Plonky2 and the zkEVMs can prove a whole CPU. It builds LOGUP (Häbök's log-derivative argument) as a full non-interactive KZG SNARK on the lab's own BLS12-381 pairing — the identity Σ 1/(β−fᵢ) = Σ mⱼ/(β−tⱼ) (with mⱼ the multiplicity of table row tⱼ) cleared of denominators into a per-row constraint over a multiplicative domain, a grand-sum accumulator that telescopes over the domain cycle, a quotient Q = (C + α·L₀·S)/Z_H committing f, m, S, Q, and a verifier re-checking the identity at one Fiat–Shamir point ζ from six openings folded into a single pairing — plus PLOOKUP (Gabizon–Williamson) in its transparent multiset-equality form (sort f∪t by the table into s, then (1+β)ⁿ∏(γ+fᵢ)∏(γ(1+β)+tᵢ+β·tᵢ₊₁) = ∏(γ(1+β)+sᵢ+β·sᵢ₊₁) iff f ⊆ t), an n-bit RANGE CHECK, and a vector XOR TABLE (rows (x,y,x⊕y) folded to x+γy+γ²(x⊕y) so a tuple lookup becomes a scalar logUp) — with a live lab showing the multiplicity histogram, the grand-sum accumulator across the domain, the KZG commitments, and soundness toggles that reject an out-of-table value and a tampered opening. All computed live in the browser, pinned to published test vectors, with zero crypto dependencies.
